content.value_statement: Teams often add tests too late or cover implementation details instead of behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to write focused Pest tests for critical paths.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Pest tests in tests/Feature and tests/Unit directories.
Prioritizes core user workflows, business logic, validation rules, and API endpoints.
Encourages descriptive test names that describe expected behavior.
Supports mocking external dependencies such as databases, APIs, file systems, and services.
Recommends Pest datasets for repeated scenarios and fast unit tests.
limitations: It provides testing guidance and does not run tests by itself.
It assumes projects use Pest and a PHP or Laravel-style test structure.
Detailed standards are linked outside the skill package, so local availability may vary.
It does not define complete coverage requirements for every project.

use_cases.title: Add Feature Coverage
use_cases.description: Create focused tests for a new user workflow before a feature is completed.

use_cases.title: Review Critical Paths
use_cases.description: Identify business rules, validation behavior, and API endpoints that need reliable tests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Pest Style
use_cases.description: Align generated tests around clear names, behavior assertions, mocks, and datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Pest tests for this small feature. Focus on the main success path and one important failure path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a narrow feature.

prompt_templates.title: Cover User Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this user workflow and propose focused Pest feature tests for its critical behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Mock External Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Write Pest tests for this service interaction. Mock external dependencies and assert observable behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Completion Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this completed feature and define the minimum strategic Pest coverage before release.

output_examples.input: Ask for tests covering registration validation and successful account creation.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes focused feature tests for required fields, invalid email input, duplicate accounts, and successful registration behavior.

output_examples.input: Ask for unit tests around a pricing rule with several scenarios.
output_examples.output: The assistant suggests concise Pest unit tests using datasets for discounts, default pricing, edge cases, and expected totals.

output_examples.input: Ask whether a completed API feature has enough coverage.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists critical endpoint behavior, validation failures, authorization cases, and external dependency mocks to add before release.

best_practices: Start with the highest-value user workflow before adding edge-case coverage.
Test observable behavior and outcomes instead of private implementation details.
Use mocks and datasets when they make tests faster and clearer.
anti_patterns: Do not generate broad snapshot tests when targeted assertions would be clearer.
Do not test private methods instead of public behavior.
Do not skip critical business paths because they require setup.

faq.question: Which test framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Pest tests, especially in PHP and Laravel-style projects.

faq.question: Can it write both feature and unit tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It references tests/Feature and tests/Unit workflows.

faq.question: Does it run the test suite?
faq.answer: No. It guides test writing and recommends running tests before committing changes.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the feature behavior, relevant files, business rules, and any external dependencies.

faq.question: Does it help decide coverage scope?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on critical paths, validation, business logic, and release completion checks.

faq.question: Is the skill self-contained?
faq.answer: Partially. It links to a detailed standard outside the skill directory, which should be bundled for reliable distribution.
